top_choice_rationale: Targeted protein degradation (Crews, Deshaies, Handa) is a designable chemical principle: a small molecule induces a ternary complex between a chosen protein and an E3 ligase, turning occupancy-driven inhibition into event-driven removal. The mechanism is quantitative (cooperativity, kinetics, structure), independently reproduced, and already validated in patients through cereblon-dependent glue drugs, so the missing approved PROTAC does not make the principle premature. A citation worded around induced proximity covers both PROTACs and glues. The omission of Ciulli, Sakamoto, Kim, Gray and Ito is a cost of the three-laureate limit, not a merit judgement. Buchwald and Hartwig C-N coupling is mature and cleanly attributed but extends the 2010 palladium paradigm, so I rank it second and above no award.
